subject.title: Add multi-gateway cron job coordination for HA deployments

question: Should OpenClaw support active-active multi-Gateway cron ownership in core, and should the permanent boundary be a backend-neutral lease interface, one bundled coordination backend, or a documented single-active-cron-Gateway deployment model?
rationale: The source establishes the missing capability, but repository policy and distributed-systems constraints do not determine the intended ownership model, outage behavior, dependency boundary, or operator contract.

options.title: Define a neutral lease seam
options.body: Add a core ownership and fencing contract with the current single-Gateway default, then connect approved backends through a narrow extension boundary.

options.title: Bundle one backend
options.body: Choose and support a core backend such as Redis, accepting its dependency, secrets, health, and upgrade obligations.

options.title: Require one cron Gateway
options.body: Document and enforce that HA deployments designate exactly one cron-enabled Gateway while other Gateway instances disable cron.

recommendation.title: Define a neutral lease seam
recommendation.body: Add a core ownership and fencing contract with the current single-Gateway default, then connect approved backends through a narrow extension boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review involvement and repeated central cron refactors make steipete the strongest available routing candidate for this architecture decision.
